description: This topic provides a detailed overview of crucial ancient and medieval books of India along with their authors. It is an essential and highly scoring segment of Static GK for competitive exams.

sections.title: Ancient Indian Treatises
sections.description: Fundamental ancient texts of India based on statecraft, grammar, and medical science.

key_associations.extra_info: A comprehensive treatise on Mauryan administration, political science, economic policy, and military strategy.
It is the most ancient and authoritative text on Sanskrit grammar, setting the linguistic standards for Classical Sanskrit.
A detailed commentary on Panini's Ashtadhyayi, further elaborating on the rules of Sanskrit grammar.
A foundational text on ancient Indian medical science and Ayurveda.
An ancient Sanskrit text primarily dealing with medicine and surgery; Sushruta is widely known as the 'Father of Plastic Surgery'.

sections.title: Classical Sanskrit Literature
sections.description: Immortal literary masterpieces composed by the great poets and dramatists of ancient India.

key_associations.extra_info: The epic love story of King Dushyanta and Shakuntala. Kalidasa's other famous works include Meghaduta, Kumarasambhava, and Raghuvamsha.
Translates to 'The Little Clay Cart'. It provides a realistic depiction of society during the Gupta period.
Narrates the political ascent of Chandragupta Maurya, the downfall of the Nanda dynasty, and Chanakya's brilliant diplomacy.
A beautiful poetic description of the divine love between Lord Krishna and Radha.
A world-renowned ancient Indian collection of interrelated animal fables designed to teach moral science and statecraft.

sections.title: Historical Chronicles and Biographies
sections.description: Crucial books documenting the history of Indian kings, regional dynasties, and their reigns.

key_associations.extra_info: Composed in Sanskrit in the 12th century, it is a historical chronicle describing the History of Kashmir and its rulers.
The biography of King Harshavardhana, widely regarded as the first historical biography in Sanskrit literature.
A romantic Sanskrit prose masterpiece, often cited as one of the world's first novels.
An epic poem written in Brajbhasha that glorifies the life, valor, and romantic tales of the Rajput king Prithviraj Chauhan.

sections.title: Medieval and Mughal Era Books
sections.description: Major historical works written by rulers, courtiers, and scholars during the Sultanate and Mughal periods.

key_associations.extra_info: The autobiography of Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire in India, originally written in the Chagatai Turkic language.
Written by Humayun's half-sister, it provides a vivid account of the life of Mughal royal family members.
A detailed official history of Akbar's reign, written in Persian, detailing administration, culture, and army.
Written in Arabic in the 11th century, it is a brilliant and extensive account of Indian society, religion, and sciences.

sections.title: Accounts of Foreign Travellers
sections.description: Invaluable books and records written by foreign ambassadors and pilgrims who visited ancient India.

key_associations.extra_info: Provides a Greek perspective on the civil administration, society, and geography of the Mauryan Empire and its capital Pataliputra.

key_associations.item: Si-Yu-Ki (The Record of the Western Regions)
key_associations.extra_info: A detailed Chinese record of his monumental journey to India during the reign of King Harshavardhana.
A travelogue written by the famous Moroccan traveller, presenting a lively account of India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

sections.title: Important Facts
sections.description: Some of the most crucial and frequently asked one-liner facts related to historical books.

important_facts.fact: Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini' is widely considered the first truly authentic and chronological historical text of India.
Vishnu Sharma's 'Panchatantra' has been translated into over 50 languages, making it one of the most translated non-religious books in the world after the Bible.
Kalidasa is often referred to as the 'Shakespeare of India' due to his extraordinary contributions to classical Sanskrit literature and drama.
The Persian translation of the ancient Upanishads was commissioned by the Mughal prince Dara Shikoh under the title 'Sirr-i-Akbar' (The Great Secret).
